<!-- pr-reviewer: 6815b21d85f8b0ef0b09a17adc63d5f6a323dde5 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Delta review of the hand-resolved refresh merge `6815b21d8` (main `1c0152c91`), the only new commit after the clean-reviewed head `576ae8081` / delta-reviewed `201b942e4`. This is a safety-tier review: the PR changes posted output (the tool-table refusal in the two Heidenhain posts).

## What looks good

- The merge keeps both sides in `script_props`: the `arcTolerance` block (main, #4161) and this PR's `toolNumberMax` block, each with its own closing brace. I read the file at the head: `crates/post/src/post/machine_installation.rs:75-93`. The PR's `FACT_KEYS`, `checked_input`, `mirror` and the two posts are consistent with the merged main.
- `max_tool_number` uses a checked integer conversion (`u32::try_from`) and refuses a bad value by name; `TOOL 254` posts and `TOOL 255` is refused by both posts through the raw file and the parsed mirror, pinned by `heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_tool_number_above_the_machine_tool_table`.
- The DIN post uses the same `typeof machine !== "undefined"` guard as the neighbouring checks; the Klartext post's `onOpen` already refuses a profile-less machine, so its unguarded `machine.toolNumberMax` read is safe.
- The decision record (`docs/decisions/4087-tool-table-max.md`) records the 254 source, the dropped alternatives and the cost to change later; no goldens, snapshots or process files are touched.

## Results merged with main

Trial merge: `6815b21d` with `origin/main` `1c0152c91` is already up to date (no conflicts). Built locally in `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4164-review` with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

A self-hosted runner run was started (`pr-test.yml` run `45887268628` for head `6815b21d8`) but it was cancelled after ~40 minutes of the Quick gate step with no output, so it gave no verdict. The local suites below are the review's verdict.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post` lib | 161 passed, 0 failed |
| `machine_controller` (touched test, post) | 6 passed, 0 failed |
| `script_heidenhain` | 16 passed, 0 failed |
| `script_heidenhain_klartext` | 27 passed, 0 failed |
| `example_catalog` (app) | 44 passed, 4 ignored (as declared), 0 failed |
| `example_catalog_adaptive` (app) | 1 passed |
| `example_catalog_edge_work` (app) | 1 passed |
| `machine_controller` (app) | 3 passed |
| `klartext_builtin` (app) | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean, no warnings |
| `cargo xtask gate light` (release, 6 steps) | 6 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 7.6 min |

The quick plan maps this diff to 344 steps (a post diff fans out to the app suites through the gate map). I ran the touched suites by name, not the full fan-out; the author's body names the full `cargo xtask gate quick` green on this head (341 steps, 0 failed).

## Targeted tests

- Example catalog suites: run, green (above) - the PR changes a post and a machine file.
- Light lane: run, green (above).
- Heavy step: none. This is a P3 PR (issue #4087), not a P1 under the safety floor, so no targeted heavy step is owed. The author's body names a heavy gate green on this head (72 steps, 0 failed) as its own evidence.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `crates/post/src/machine/def.rs` (433 lines) and `crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs` (439 lines) are both past the ~400-line limit. Pre-existing, not caused by this PR (it adds ~8 lines to each). Consider a later split.
- Optional, non-blocking: the follow-up from the earlier delta review (a test that a file-form input stating only `tooling.max_tool_number` produces `toolNumberMax` in the script, and that a mixed input is refused by `check_input_form`) still stands. The tool-255 and 254 pins cover the refusal path through both inputs, not the `script_props` block's own attachment.
- The app's own machine validator (`crates/app/src/machine/validate.rs`) still does not judge `max_tool_number`; the reader refuses a bad value at load. The PR body already states this.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
